title: Arnold Palmer: Layered Iced Tea and Lemonade
summary: Black tea is brewed and chilled, lemonade is made from lemon zest mashed with sugar, hot water and fresh juice, then the two are layered over ice.

ingredients.item: black tea bags, such as English Breakfast (about 8 g)

steps.title: Brew the tea
steps.text: Pour the boiled water over the tea bags, steep for 5 minutes, then discard the bags. Cool to room temperature, about 30 minutes, then chill.

steps.title: Make lemon sugar
steps.text: Peel the zest from the 2 scrubbed lemons in strips, avoiding the white pith, and mash it with the sugar in the bowl for 2 minutes until damp and very fragrant. The sugar pulls the oils out of the zest.

steps.title: Finish the lemonade
steps.text: Stir in the hot water until the sugar dissolves, then add the lemon juice and cold water. Strain into a jug, pressing on the zest, and chill.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Fill 6 tall glasses with ice and pour in lemonade to half way. Slowly pour the cold tea over the back of a spoon so it floats on top. Garnish with a lemon round.

tips: The tea must be cold before layering, or it mixes straight into the lemonade.
Pouring over the back of a spoon spreads the tea gently so the layers stay separate.
For a pitcher version, simply mix equal amounts of tea and lemonade.
English Breakfast or any brisk black tea works well.
storage: Keep the tea and lemonade separate, covered, in the fridge for up to 3 days. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
